blocks.text: They have leaders at the head of the column and οὐραγοὺς [ouragous] at the rear, whom the Philosopher describes as ἐπισυρίττοντας ἐν τοῖς ἐσχάτοις, ὥστε ἀκούεσθαι τὴν φωνὴν [episyrittontas en tois eschatois, hōste akouesthai tēn phōnēn], whistling among the hindmost, so that their voice can be heard. Hence Pliny: They choose a leader to follow. At the rear of the column they have birds posted to call out in turn and to keep the flock together with their voice. And Solinus: Confident of its course, it goes before the flocks and rebukes sluggishness in flight with its voice, which keeps the column together. When that voice has grown hoarse, another takes its place. Aelian asserts that the older birds, experienced in the routes, are ἡγεμόνας τῆς πτήσεως [hēgemonas tēs ptēseōs], leaders of the flight, and that they οὐραγεῖν [ouragein], that is, command the rear of the column, while the younger ones are in the middle. [II, 624] Especially remarkable is the way they help one another in flight. Cicero: They rest their necks and heads on the backs of those flying in front. Because the leader himself cannot do this, since he has nothing to lean on, he flies back so that he too may rest. His place is taken by the nearest of those that have been resting, and this alternation is kept up throughout the whole journey. Basil, Hexaëmeron, Homily 8: Ἄλλό τε γὰρ ἄλλη τὴν ὁδηγίαν ἐκδέχεται, καὶ τακτόν τινα χρόνον προκαθηγησαμένη τῆς πτήσεως, εἰς τὸ κατόπιν περιελθοῦσα, τῇ μεθ᾽ ἑαυτὴν τὴν ἡγεμονίαν τῆς ὁδοῦ παραδίδωσι [Allo te gar allē tēn hodēgian ekdechetai, kai takton tina chronon prokathēgēsamenē tēs ptēseōs, eis to katopin perielthousa, tē meth᾽ heautēn tēn hēgemonian tēs hodou paradidōsi]. Hence Ambrose, Hexaëmeron, book 5, chapter 15: One goes before the rest for a set time and, as it were, runs ahead of the standards; then it turns back and yields the office of leading the column to the one following. Cassiodorus, book 9, Letter 2: Their flight, too, is arranged by an equal alternation: the last becomes first, and the one that held first place does not refuse to be behind. Damir the Arab: يقدمها واحد منها كالرايس لها وهي [yuqaddimuhā wāḥid minhā ka-l-rāyis lahā wa-hiya] [col. 75] تتبعه ويكون ذلك حينا ثم يخلفه اخر منها مقدما حتي يصير الذي كان مقدما موخرا [tatbaʿuhu wa-yakūnu dhālika ḥīnan thumma yakhlufuhu ākhar minhā muqaddaman ḥattā yaṣīra alladhī kāna muqaddaman muʾakhkharan] One of them goes ahead, acting as leader, and the others follow, and this for a time. Then another from their number takes its place, until the one that had been first becomes last.
